# `fluxsim verify`

Re-check an applied run on five independent legs: the run's own artifacts against its recorded digest, the golden regression, row conformance against the referenced contract, the RFC-04 enforcement vectors, and every declared fidelity check. One line per leg, with the flag that turns a `not checked` leg into a result. A run whose plan pins a profile is also scored against it, per property, table, dimension and overall, when the profile is passed with --profile. A bundle that declares consumer queries has every query counted on the run, the calibration queries apart from the held-out ones (--held-out), in the scorecard's queries dimension. Each counts entry of the bundle adds the rule lines counts:&lt;relationship&gt;.minChildren and counts:&lt;relationship&gt;.parentWhen to the child's rules, both enforced, and a profile that publishes the children per parent of a relationship adds a childrenPerParent row to the scorecard.

## Synopsis

```text
fluxsim verify [options] <bundle>
```

## Examples

```bash
# re-check an applied run on five independent legs
fluxsim verify ./bundle --run-id de72fa4b22711c52
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

## Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--run-id` | `RUN_ID` | the run id to act on (as reported by `fluxsim plan`/`fluxsim run`) **(required)** |
| `--update-golden` |  | record this run as the golden baseline (requires --reason) |
| `--reason` | `REASON` | why the golden baseline is being updated |
| `--committed-slice` | `EXPOSE_ID=file://PATH` | the committed real-data slice one expose's fidelity check is measured against, as EXPOSE_ID=file://PATH; repeatable, once per expose; the file holds one JSON object per line, keyed by the expose's contract column names (e.g. {"subscriber_id": "s-1", "amount": "12.50"}) |
| `--profile` | `PATH` | the profile document this run's plan pins (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md): every declared fidelity property with no --committed-slice is checked against it, and the run is scored per property, table, dimension and overall (docs/spec/SCORECARD-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the run pins none |
| `--sample` | `FRACTION` | compare each emit's means, histograms and quantile bins with the pinned profile on a sample: FRACTION of its blocks of records, each estimate decided by its 95 per cent interval (docs/spec/SAMPLE-SPEC.md) |
| `--sample-block` | `N` | records in a block of the sample (default: 1000); needs --sample |
| `--sample-seed` | `N` | seed of the choice of blocks (default: 0); needs --sample |
| `--vectors` | `VECTORS` | path to an RFC-04 vectors file |
| `--allow-declared-baseline-drift` |  | exit 0 even when the bundle's declared golden.baselineDigest does not match this run's runDigest |
| `--signing-key` | `SIGNING_KEY` | file holding the 32-byte ed25519 seed a prior `fluxsim ship` signed with; its public half becomes the trust anchor, and the check says it is self-attested |
| `--trust-key` | `PATH` | file holding the 32-byte raw ed25519 PUBLIC key (raw or hex -- the `publicKey` a fidelity record prints) any fidelity record this run already holds is checked against; without it, and without --signing-key, the signature is reported as not checked |
| `--jobs` | `N` | the most processes that may read the run's emits at once, one emit to a process: a number or auto for one per CPU; the verdicts and every byte of the scorecard are the same whatever the number (default: FLUX_JOBS, else 1) |
| `--held-out` | `FILE` | the held-out profile: a profile document whose queries section holds the targets of the bundle's held-out consumer queries, which the pinned profile may not name; it is graded beside the pinned profile and read by nothing else |
| `--max-query-seconds` | `N` | raise the seconds one consumer query may take above the engine's 30, up to 600, for a bundle that declares no limits.seconds; a bundle's own value is kept and may only lower the ceiling |
| `--max-query-memory` | `SIZE` | raise the memory DuckDB may use for the consumer queries above the engine's 1GiB, up to 16GiB, such as 4GiB, for a bundle that declares no limits.memory; a bundle's own value is kept and may only lower the ceiling |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
